title: 5 Reasons to Invest in an HVAC Maintenance Plan
desc: We all want our HVAC systems to work as efficiently as possible for as long as possible, learn the best way to make this happen.

blocks.text: Your HVAC equipment keeps your living space comfortable all year round. It keeps your residential property warm in the wet winter months and cool in the summer. Therefore, it’s important to keep the unit in good condition by having all the components inspected and cleaned by a certified HVAC technician every year.

An HVAC technician can easily detect minor problems within the unit before they grow into major issues that need costly repairs or emergency replacements. Besides, with high replacement costs and the shortage of HVAC parts and components, keeping your HVAC equipment operating well should be one of the top items on your priority list. A maintenance plan will keep the unit running optimally and more efficiently for many years. Here are more reasons to invest in a good maintenance plan for your HVAC.
1. Reliable Equipment

Having your HVAC serviced in fall and spring plays a major role in your residential property’s comfort because it makes your HVAC reliable throughout the year. The last thing you want is a heater, furnace, or air conditioner at risk of breaking down when you need it the most.

A maintenance plan allows HVAC experts to inspect, service, and clean the entire system fully. During routine maintenance visits, these professionals can identify any potential problems and rectify small issues before they become big problems. This way, you’ll prevent premature failures that leave you without a working system in rough weather.
2. Lower Energy Bills

While ignoring or skipping HVAC maintenance may not have immediate adverse effects, it affects your equipment’s performance and efficiency in the long run. Heating units and air conditioners normally accumulate wear and tear over the years, decreasing your HVAC unit’s efficiency. According to statistics, an HVAC loses about 5% of its energy efficiency each year you skip maintenance, leading to increased utility bills.

Enrolling in a biannual or yearly maintenance plan can help keep the cooling and heating equipment operating at 95% of its efficiency throughout its lifecycle. When your heat pump, furnace, or air conditioning unit operates optimally, it’ll run more efficiently. And more efficiency means the HVAC equipment will consume minimal energy, keeping your monthly utility bills down irrespective of the season.
3. Extends HVAC Service Life

Your cooling and heating appliances work around the clock to ensure you have a comfortable indoor environment. Nonetheless, you can’t expect your furnace, heat pump, or air conditioners to work that hard without good maintenance. An air conditioning unit or heating system that breaks down several years before its expected lifespan only means an expensive unit replacement.

Research studies indicate that a maintenance arrangement that involves annual servicing can extend your HVAC unit’s service life by up to 50%. The better you maintain your cooling and heating system, the better it will take care of your home, and the longer it’ll last. Ensure routine maintenance for the highest return on investment of your home’s HVAC system.
4. Improves Air Quality

Research studies indicate that air pollutants levels within the house can be two to five times greater than the outdoor levels. Exposure to polluted air for a long period can make you and your family vulnerable to various health problems, including eye irritation, regular headaches, respiratory complications, and cardiovascular disease.

If you want to boost air quality, consider investing in a good HVAC maintenance plan. During routine maintenance, the technicians will inspect and clean all the components, change HVAC air filters, and check your ductwork for leaks to ensure clean airflow.
5. Keeps Your HVAC Unit’s Warranty Valid

Extended warranties cover labor and the major parts of your HVAC system, providing a long-term protection arrangement for the unit. These warranties require you to have an annual HVAC maintenance plan. Therefore, you should have an HVAC professional inspect, service, and clean your cooling and heating equipment yearly to keep your warranty valid.

Ignoring your warranty can lead to problems, especially if you need to address unforeseen and expensive repairs. Generally, many HVAC experts and manufacturers require proof of annual maintenance, particularly when submitting repair claims.
